chunks: Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Abu Isma'il al-Sarraj, from Bishr ibn Ja'far, from Mufaddal ibn 'Umar, from Abu Abdullah (عليه السلام), who said:

I heard him saying, 'Do you know what the shirt of Yusuf (عليه السلام) was?' He said: I said, 'No.' He said: 'When the fire was kindled for Ibrahim (عليه السلام), Jibra'il (عليه السلام) came to him with a garment from the garments of Paradise and clothed him with it, so neither heat nor cold harmed him while it was with him.'

Then when death came before Ibrahim, he placed it in an amulet and hung it upon Ishaq, and Ishaq hung it upon Ya'qub. Then when Yusuf (عليه السلام) was born, he hung it upon him, and it remained on his upper arm until there occurred of his affair what occurred. Then when Yusuf brought it out from the amulet in Egypt, Ya'qub sensed its scent.
And it is His saying: 'Indeed, I surely find the scent of Yusuf, were it not that you would deem me senile.'
So that was the shirt which Allah sent down from Paradise.

I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, then to whom did that shirt pass?' He said, 'To its people.' Then he said, 'Every Prophet who left inherited knowledge or something else, it has indeed ended up with the family of Muhammad (صلى الله عليه وآله).'

key_terms.آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ: The family of Muhammad (صلى الله عليه وآله), described as the final inheritors of prophetic legacy.
key_terms.تَمِيمَةٍ: An amulet or protective wrapping in which the garment was placed.
key_terms.ثِيَابِ الْجَنَّةِ: Garments of Paradise, indicating the shirt's celestial origin.
key_terms.رِيحَ يُوسُفَ: The scent of Yusuf (عليه السلام) perceived by Ya'qub (عليه السلام).
key_terms.قَمِيصُ يُوسُفَ: The shirt of Yusuf (عليه السلام), identified here as a heavenly garment passed down through prophets.

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about the shirt of Yusuf (عليه السلام) and how did it reach آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ (صلى الله عليه وآله)?
ai.summary: This narration explains that the shirt associated with Yusuf (عليه السلام) was originally a garment from Paradise given to Ibrahim (عليه السلام) and passed down through the prophets until it reached Yusuf (عليه السلام). It also connects the scent perceived by Ya'qub (عليه السلام) to that heavenly garment and concludes that the inherited knowledge and relics of the prophets ultimately came to آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ (صلى الله عليه وآله).

en.hubeali:
Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Al Husay, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Abu Ismail Al Sarraj, from Bishr Bin Ja’far, from Mufazzal Bin Umar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I heard him<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Do you know what was the shirt of Yusuf<sup>as</sup>?’ I said, ‘No’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Ibrahim<sup>as</sup>, when the fire was inflamed for him<sup>as</sup>, Jibraeel<sup>as</sup> came over to him<sup>as</sup> with a cloth from the clothes of the Paradise. So he<sup>as</sup> wore it, and with it, the heat and the cold did not harm him<sup>as</sup>.

So when the death presented itself to Ibrahimas, heas made it to be in an amulet and hung it upon Is’haqas, and Is’haqas hung it upon Yaqoub. So when Yusufas was born, heas hung it upon himas. Thus, it was on hisas shoulder until it was from hisas affair which was. So when Yusufas took it out from the amulet in Egypt, Yaqoubas found its smell, and these are hisas words [12:94] Surely I find the aroma of Yusuf, unless you pronounce me to be weak minded.
So it was that shirt which Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Sent down from the Paradise’

I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! So to whom has that shirt come to be?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘To its rightful ones’. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Every Prophet<sup>as</sup> inherited knowledge or something else, so it has ended up to the Progeny<sup>asws</sup> of Muhammad<sup>saww</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Isma‘il al-Sarraj from Bishr ibn Ja‘far from Mufaddal ibn ‘Umar who has said that he heard abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) say the following.

“Do you know what was the shirt of Joseph?” I said, “I do not know.” The Imam (a.s.) said, “When the fire was set for Abraham, Jibril brought him a dress from paradise and made him t wear it. With that dress on him nothing of the cold or heat would harm him.

When Abraham was about to die, he placed it in a covering and hanged it to Isacc (Ishaq) who hanged to Jacob (Ya‘qub). When Joseph was born it was hanged to him and he had it on his shoulder until the event of the things that happened to this shirt. When he Joseph took it out of its covering in Egypt, Jacob (Ya’qub) felt its fragrance as he said,
““I smell Joseph’s scent. I hope that you will not accuse me of senility” [12:94].
It was the same shirt that sent from paradise.”

I then said, “May Allah take my soul in service for your cause, to who did that shirt go thereafter?” The Imam (a.s.) said, “It went to its (people) owner.” Then he said, “Every prophet who inherited knowledge or other things, they all ended to the family of Muhammad (s.a.).”
